title: Spaces Between Words
keyIdea: A space is a gap between two words. It shows where one word stops and the next one starts, so the reader can tell the words apart. mydogruns is hard to read; my dog runs is easy. When writing, children put a finger down after each word to make a finger space. Spaces go between words, never inside a word: d og is wrong, dog is right. A line always has one more word than spaces.
familyTip: When you read a picture book together, point to each word as you say it, one touch per word. Then write a short line such as 'we can hop' with no spaces and ask your child to show you where the gaps should go. When they write, remind them: word, finger, word.

visual.caption: Are the spaces right, or not? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: count words by tapping them, open finger spaces in squashed lines, close gaps inside words, write with a finger-space card and check a note.

kid: We put a gap between words. It is called a space. The space shows where one word stops. Then the next word starts.
Look at mydogruns. It is hard to read! Now look at my dog runs. The spaces show us three words.
When you write, put a finger down after each word. That makes a finger space. Then write the next word.
Do not put a space in the middle of a word. d og is wrong. dog is one word, so keep it all together.
adult: Ages 4 to 6. The National Curriculum in England asks Year 1 pupils to leave spaces between words when they write (English Appendix 2 lists 'separation of words with spaces' under Year 1 punctuation). In the US, Common Core RF.K.1c asks kindergarteners to understand that words are separated by spaces in print, and L.K.2 covers early capitals, punctuation and spelling in writing.

Spacing rests on knowing what a word is, called word awareness or the concept of a word in print (Marie Clay's Concepts About Print checks it). Many young children cannot yet tell a letter from a word, so they count letters when asked for words or read a squashed line as one long word. Pointing to each printed word as you say it, one touch per spoken word, builds that link.

Common mistakes: running words together (mydogruns), putting a space inside a word (d og), leaving a gap after every letter, and gaps so wide the line looks like a list. The finger space, the width of the child's own finger or a lolly-stick 'spaceman', is a widely used prompt that fades as handwriting gets even. A useful check: a line has one more word than spaces.

In the lab your child taps each word to count words rather than letters, taps between letters to open spaces in three squashed lines, closes gaps that cut a word in two, writes two lines by dragging a word, a finger space and the next word, and checks a note that has both slips.

practice.prompt: Which line has the spaces right?
practice.hint: Look for one gap between each pair of words.
practice.explain: I like cake. has a space after I and after like. Ilikecake. is squashed, and li ke cuts like in two.

practice.prompt: A line has {n} words. How many spaces go between them?
practice.hint: There is no space after the last word.
practice.explain: {n} words need {=n-1} spaces, one between each pair of words.

practice.prompt: How many words? the sun is hot
practice.hint: Touch each word as you say it: the, sun ...
practice.explain: the, sun, is, hot: 4 words. 11 is the number of letters, not words.

practice.prompt: Sam writes {a} words on one line and {b} words on the next line. How many words does he write?
practice.hint: Add the words on both lines.

practice.prompt: Where should the space go in mydog?
practice.explain: my and dog are two words, so the space goes after my: my dog.

pool.prompt: What does a space between words show?
choices: Where one word stops and the next starts
pool.hint: Think of mydogruns and my dog runs.
pool.explain: A space marks the end of one word and the start of the next, so you can tell the words apart.

pool.hint: Every word needs its own room, and no word is cut.
pool.explain: we can hop has a space between each word. wecan is squashed and ca n cuts can in two.

pool.prompt: A sentence has {n} words. How many finger spaces do you need?
pool.hint: A finger goes after each word except the last one.
pool.explain: {n} words need {=n-1} finger spaces, because the last word has none after it.

pool.prompt: How many words? a big red bus
pool.hint: Count the words, not the letters.
pool.explain: a, big, red, bus: 4 words. 11 is the letters.

pool.prompt: When you write, what do you put down after each word?
choices: A finger, to make a space
pool.hint: It makes a gap before the next word.
pool.explain: A finger after each word makes a finger space. A full stop only goes at the end of the sentence.

pool.prompt: Which word is cut in two? the c at sat
pool.hint: Find bits that are not a word on their own.
pool.explain: c at should be cat. A space must not go inside a word.

pool.prompt: A line has {s} spaces between its words. How many words does it have?
pool.hint: There is always one more word than spaces.

pool.explain: thecatsat has no spaces, so the three words run together.

pool.hint: Read it slowly and listen for each word.
pool.explain: fun, in, the, sun are four words, so it needs three spaces: fun in the sun.

pool.prompt: Mia writes mydog with no space. What should she do?
choices: Leave a finger space after my
pool.hint: The words need a gap between them.
pool.explain: A finger space after my gives my dog. Small letters that touch are still squashed.
